name: Serengeti National Park
region: Mara and Simiyu regions, northern Tanzania
tagline: Endless golden plains, the greatest wildlife spectacle on Earth and some of the best lion and leopard viewing in Africa.
highlight: Watching a river crossing or a lion pride at sunrise from an open safari vehicle.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed park of 14,750 square kilometres, home to the Great Migration of wildebeest and zebra, big cats, balloon safaris and classic acacia-dotted savannah.
metaDescription: A Serengeti safari guide: the Great Migration by season, Seronera, the northern Kogatende crossings, balloon safaris, camps versus lodges, costs and a four-day plan.
nearestAirport: Kilimanjaro (JRO) or Arusha (ARK), with light-aircraft flights to airstrips in the park
knownFor: Wildlife, the Great Migration, big cats
budget: US$350-900+ per person per day, safari

image.alt: A hot-air balloon rising over the Serengeti plains at dawn

intro: The Serengeti is Tanzania's oldest and most famous national park, a World Heritage Site covering a vast ecosystem of open grassland, kopjes (rocky outcrops), riverine forest and woodland. The name comes from the Maasai word for "endless plains", and standing on them at dawn it is easy to see why.

The park is best known for the Great Migration, in which around 1.5 million wildebeest, along with hundreds of thousands of zebra and gazelle, travel in a loop through the ecosystem in search of fresh grass. Calving takes place on the southern plains in January to March, the herds head north through the western corridor and the centre, and the dramatic Mara River crossings in the north usually happen between July and October. Even outside the migration the park holds one of the densest populations of lions, leopards, cheetahs and elephants in Africa.

Safaris here are done in 4x4 vehicles with pop-up roofs, with game drives at dawn and late afternoon. Seronera in the centre is the most reliable base year-round, while the northern Kogatende area and the western corridor follow the herds. Budget time and money for a stay of at least three to four nights, since distances are long and the best viewing is early and late in the day.

whyVisit.intro: The Serengeti offers wildlife viewing on a scale few places can match.

attractionsIntro: The park is divided into regions, and where you go depends on the season.

attractions.name: Seronera Valley

image.file: File:002 Male Lion prowling in the Serengeti National Park Photo by Giles Laurent.jpg
image.alt: A male lion prowling in the Serengeti

attractions.text: The central hub, with permanent water and the best year-round predator viewing, especially leopards in the riverine trees.
attractions.tip: Go out before breakfast, when cats are still active.

attractions.name: Southern plains (Ndutu area)

image.file: File:Zebras in Serengeti National Park with Acacia tree.jpg
image.alt: Zebras beside an acacia tree on the Serengeti plains

attractions.text: Calving grounds of the wildebeest, from about January to March, with predators on the hunt.
attractions.tip: Book early, since camps are small and in demand.

attractions.name: Western Corridor (Grumeti)
attractions.text: Crocodile-filled river crossings in May to July as the herds move north.
attractions.tip: Crossing timing varies from year to year.

attractions.name: Kogatende and the Mara River
attractions.text: Dramatic river crossings, usually July to October, in the far north.
attractions.tip: Allow several nights and patience for the crossing.

attractions.name: Moru Kopjes
attractions.text: Granite outcrops with rock paintings and Maasai history, and rare black rhino.

attractions.name: Retina Hippo Pool
attractions.text: A pool packed with hippos, a short walk from the vehicle with a ranger.

thingsToDoIntro: Safari days are built around early starts and long drives.

thingsToDo.title: Take a sunrise game drive
thingsToDo.text: Leave camp before dawn when predators are active.
thingsToDo.tip: Pack a layer, since mornings are cold.

thingsToDo.title: Float in a hot-air balloon
thingsToDo.text: A silent flight over the plains, followed by a bush breakfast.
thingsToDo.tip: Book ahead, as flights can be cancelled in bad weather.

thingsToDo.title: Watch a river crossing
thingsToDo.text: In the north, wait at the Mara River for the herds to cross.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring patience and a packed lunch.

thingsToDo.title: Join a walking safari
thingsToDo.text: With an armed ranger in permitted areas.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a Maasai village
thingsToDo.text: Learn about pastoral life and buy crafts.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph at the kopjes
thingsToDo.text: Lions rest on granite outcrops at midday.
thingsToDo.tip: Use a bean bag for steady shots.

gettingThere.intro: Most visitors fly to the park or drive from Arusha.

options.text: About 1 to 1.5 hours to Seronera, with charter and scheduled flights.
options.detail: The easiest option, saves a long drive.
Often combined with the crater on the way.

options.text: Small aircraft link Arusha with several airstrips.
options.detail: Baggage limits apply, with soft bags only.

gettingAround.intro: You will use a safari vehicle, almost always with a driver-guide.

options.text: Only with a ranger, in designated areas.

bestTime.headline: June-October
bestTime.summary: The dry season from June to October is the classic time for river crossings and easier game viewing.

seasons.text: Calving season on the southern plains, with predators and green grass.
Dry weather, migration in the north and top wildlife viewing.
Long rains, lower prices and fewer vehicles.
Short rains, herds moving south and lush landscapes.

bestTime.avoid: April and May, when rains can make roads difficult.

tipsIntro: A few tips make safari life easier.
tips: Book well ahead for July to October and for calving season.
Pack neutral clothing and layers, since dawn is cold.
Bring binoculars and a camera with a long lens.
Use soft bags for light-aircraft flights.
Tip your guide and camp staff.
Never leave the vehicle except where permitted.
